verses.text: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
Uzziah rebuilt the town of Elath and won it back for Judah after his father died.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Amaziah had done.
He looked to God while Zechariah was alive, a man who taught him to respect God. As long as he looked to the LORD, God made him successful.
He went to war against the Philistines and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. He built towns near Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia.
God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs who lived in Gur Baal, and against the Meunites.
The Ammonites paid Uzziah tribute money. He became famous as far as the border of Egypt, because he became very powerful.
Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the corner of the wall, and he made them strong.

He also built towers in the desert and dug many water wells, because he had many cattle in the foothills and on the plains. He had people working his fields and vineyards in the hills and in the fertile lands, because he loved farming.
Uzziah had a well-trained army ready for battle, organized in groups. They were counted by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer, under the command of Hananiah, one of the king's officials.
There were two thousand six hundred family leaders in charge of these brave soldiers.
Under them was an army of three hundred seven thousand five hundred men, trained to fight with great power to help the king against his enemies.
Uzziah gave the whole army shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones for slings.

In Jerusalem he had machines made by skilled men to put on the towers and corners of the walls, to shoot arrows and throw large stones. He became famous far and wide, because God helped him in amazing ways until he became powerful.
But when Uzziah became powerful, his pride led to his downfall. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God. He went into the LORD's temple to burn incense on the incense altar.
Azariah the priest went in after him with eighty other brave priests of the LORD.

They stood up to King Uzziah and said, "Uzziah, it is not your job to burn incense to the LORD. That is the job of the priests, the descendants of Aaron, who have been set apart to burn incense. Leave the holy place, because you have been unfaithful. The LORD God will not honor you for this."

Uzziah was holding a pan for burning incense, and he became angry. While he was raging at the priests in front of the incense altar in the LORD's temple, a skin disease broke out on his forehead right in front of them.

Azariah the chief priest and all the other priests looked at him and saw the skin disease on his forehead. They hurried him out of the temple. He himself was in a hurry to leave, because the LORD had struck him.

King Uzziah had the skin disease until the day he died. He lived in a separate house, because he had the disease and was not allowed in the LORD's temple. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace and ruled the people of the land.
The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz wrote down everything else Uzziah did, from beginning to end.
Uzziah died and was buried near his ancestors in a burial field that belonged to the kings, because people said, "He had a skin disease." His son Jotham became king after him.
